summary: 14-day telemetry reveals exceptional glycemic control with 99.7% Time in Range (70–180 mg/dL), 0.0% Time Below Range (<70 mg/dL), and an average glucose of 117.0 mg/dL with a low coefficient of variation (12.9%). Overnight fasting baselines and non-meal periods remain stable, while active AAPS automation (SMB and UAM) effectively handles postprandial excursions following declared meal strategies without inducing hypoglycemia.

analysis_steps.findings: Complete 14-day CGM coverage (1,345 valid entries, 100% coverage, 0 gaps) with comprehensive treatment and active AAPS profile telemetry.
analysis_steps.evidence: 1,345 CGM readings, 0 gaps >15 minutes, 32 treatments, 28 meal boluses logged over 14 days.

analysis_steps.findings: Glycemic metrics meet clinical targets: TIR is 99.7%, TAR (>180 mg/dL) is 0.3%, and TBR (<70 mg/dL) is 0.0%. Glycemic variability is low (SD 15.1 mg/dL, CV 12.9%).
analysis_steps.evidence: glucose_summary: TIR=99.7%, TAR=0.3%, TBR=0.0%, average=117.0 mg/dL, CV=12.9%. Minimum glucose recorded is 70 mg/dL.

analysis_steps.findings: Overnight basal rates (00:00–06:00) hold glucose remarkably flat between 102 mg/dL and 112 mg/dL, matching programmed target ranges (95–110 mg/dL). Daytime non-meal baselines remain stable.
Profile Carb Ratios and ISF values effectively return glucose to baseline across all meal windows within 4 hours. DIA of 5.5 hours matches observed decay curves.
analysis_steps.evidence: Therapy response windows demonstrate 240-minute glucose changes between -11 mg/dL and +8 mg/dL post-meal.

analysis_steps.findings: SMB and UAM settings (3-minute interval, 45-minute max SMB basal, 30-minute max UAM) operate safely without stacking IOB or causing secondary hypoglycemia.
analysis_steps.evidence: 0.0% TBR, 0 entries <70 mg/dL, controlled recovery following transient post-meal rises.

analysis_steps.findings: Safety limits (max_basal 2.4 U/h, max_iob 8.0 U) provide appropriate safety margins above active basal rates (1.05 U/h max) and bolus sizes.
analysis_steps.evidence: Max programmed basal rate is 1.05 U/h, fitting well within the 2.4 U/h limit; maximum single bolus is ~5.8 U.

analysis_steps.findings: Declared prebolus strategies (20 min for breakfast, 10 min for weekend brunch) adequately manage postprandial glucose curves. Weekend brunches show temporary rises to 188 mg/dL that safely resolve by +240m.
analysis_steps.evidence: Therapy response windows: Weekday breakfast +120m rise +33 to +57 mg/dL; Weekend brunch +120m peak up to 188 mg/dL, resolving to ~115 mg/dL at +240m.

analysis_steps.findings: Weekend brunch e-carbs strategy (20g over 120m, 15m offset) allows UAM automation to effectively cover delayed fat/protein absorption without insulin stacking.
analysis_steps.evidence: Glucose returns to pre-meal levels at +240m (-11 to +1 mg/dL net change) across all brunch entries.

analysis_steps.findings: All analysis steps confirm system stability and optimal configuration. No profile, automation, or parameter changes are required. The current setup delivers exceptional control safely.
analysis_steps.evidence: 100% data completeness, 99.7% TIR, 0.0% TBR, stable fasting baselines, predictable meal recoveries.

strengths: Outstanding Time in Range (99.7%) with 0.0% Time Below Range across the entire 14-day evaluation period.
Highly stable overnight fasting glucose baselines holding between 102 mg/dL and 112 mg/dL.
Very low glycemic variability (CV 12.9%, standard deviation 15.1 mg/dL).
Well-aligned meal strategy and AAPS automation setup managing postprandial absorption without secondary lows.
issues: Transient postprandial peak up to 188 mg/dL during weekend brunches due to delayed fat/protein absorption, though safely resolved by +240 minutes.

recommendations.title: Maintain Current Profile Basal and Parameters
recommendations.description: With 99.7% TIR, flat overnight baselines, and 0.0% TBR, all profile basal rates, CR, ISF, and target segments are well-tuned and should remain unchanged.

profile_recommendation.recommendation: Keep all current active profile settings (basal rates, CR, ISF, DIA, and target ranges) unchanged.
profile_recommendation.rationale: Overall metrics demonstrate exceptional glycemic control with 99.7% TIR, 0.0% TBR, an average glucose of 117.0 mg/dL, and flat overnight fasting curves.
profile_recommendation.next_check: Re-evaluate CGM telemetry in 14 to 30 days or if routine daily schedules or meal compositions change significantly.

parameter_decisions.rationale: Overnight glucose between 00:00 and 06:00 is flat and stable (103–107 mg/dL average) with zero hypoglycemia.
Morning baseline remains stable and supports fasting periods prior to breakfast.
Afternoon glucose trajectories show predictable recovery following meal windows.
Evening baseline holds glucose steady through dinner and early night hours.
Overnight carb ratio is inactive during sleep and shows no unexpected late-night carb impacts.
Weekday breakfast boluses consistently return glucose to baseline within 4 hours (+3 to -14 mg/dL change).
Midday carb ratio accurately balances weekend brunch and lunch meals back to target at +240m.
Dinner boluses reliably return glucose to pre-meal baseline (+14 to -14 mg/dL change at +360m).
Overnight sensitivity is appropriate for automated corrections without causing lows.
Morning sensitivity matches observed correction responsiveness.
Midday sensitivity is well calibrated for SMB micro-bolus adjustments.
Evening sensitivity effectively manages post-dinner stabilization.
Target range maintains tight overnight control without hypoglycemia.
Daytime target range supports excellent TIR (99.7%).
Pre-bedtime target provides smooth transition into overnight sleep hours.
5.5 hours matches rapid-acting insulin active duration and prevents premature stacked corrections.
SMB and UAM are functioning efficiently without inducing over-delivery or hypoglycemia.
Specific activation toggles are null in telemetry; verify in AAPS preferences that SMB activation rules match intended setup.

parameter_decisions.current_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=45 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=30 min
parameter_decisions.suggested_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=45 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=30 min
parameter_decisions.rationale: 3-minute interval and basal delivery limits provide effective micro-bolus responsiveness safely.

parameter_decisions.parameter: AAPS / max basal and max IOB limits
parameter_decisions.rationale: Safety limits accommodate required automation headroom while preventing excessive insulin delivery.
Autosens toggle switches are null in raw profile telemetry; verify active sensitivity settings on device.
3 mg/dL/5min impact floor and 6-hour max absorption match observed meal absorption curves.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Maintain the current prebolus timing (15-20 minutes for breakfast, 10 minutes for brunch) and split immediate bolus percentages (60-70%) with e-carbs for higher-fat meals, allowing AAPS SMB/UAM to manage subtle postprandial variations.
meal_strategy_summary.rationale: Meal response windows demonstrate excellent recovery to pre-meal baseline within 4 hours without postprandial hypoglycemia across all logged meals.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Observe 2-hour postprandial peak glucose during weekend brunches if prebolus timing is increased slightly from 10 to 15 minutes.

exceptions.suggestion: Keep 10-minute prebolus, 60% immediate bolus, and 20g e-carbs over 120 minutes with a 15-minute start offset.
exceptions.rationale: Higher-fat brunch causes a transient peak up to 188 mg/dL at 120 minutes, but glucose smoothly returns to baseline (~115 mg/dL) by 240 minutes without hypoglycemia.

implementation_steps: No parameter or profile changes are recommended at this time.
Continue following declared meal prebolus and e-carb routines for breakfast and weekend brunch.
Optionally test extending weekend brunch prebolus timing from 10 minutes to 15 minutes to evaluate drenching the 2-hour peak.
Review raw AAPS preference toggles on device to confirm SMB and Autosens active switches.
education: Time in Range (TIR) of 70–180 mg/dL above 70% and Coefficient of Variation (CV) under 36% are key clinical metrics for diabetes management safety.
Extended carbohydrates (e-carbs) in AAPS help model delayed fat and protein absorption by feeding simulated carbs to UAM algorithm over time, avoiding early insulin stacking.
safety_notes: This analysis is decision-support content only and does not constitute medical advice.
Always consult with your healthcare team before making changes to diabetes management parameters.
Make parameter adjustments one at a time and monitor glucose outcomes closely.
